journal: J. Chem. Eng. Data 64 (6), 2484-2496; Wang, J.; et al.: Determination of CO2 Solubility in Water and NaCl Solutions under Geological Sequestration Conditions Using a Fused Silica Capillary Cell with in Situ Raman Spectroscopy
needs_pass2_reason: text layer was clean; all four tables compared against the 170 dpi page images with no discrepancy found
experimental_method: CO2-saturated water or NaCl solution is circulated through a fused silica capillary cell; the Raman nu(CO2)/nu(H2O) peak height ratio, converted with a calibration against known CO2 concentrations, gives the CO2 solubility in situ.
uncertainties_stated: u(T) = 0.01 K; u(P) = 0.039 MPa; u(b) = 0.0005 b (NaCl molality, relative); CO2 solubility uncertainty from the average deviation of five Raman ratio measurements; NaCl solutions prepared gravimetrically.
quality_remarks: Indirect (calibrated spectroscopic) determination. Authors compare water data with the Duan and Akinfiev-Diamond models (Tables 9, 10, not extracted). Pressure basis (total vs CO2 partial) not stated. Temperature scale not stated.
not_extracted_tables: Tables 2 and 3: Raman peak height ratios of calibration solutions (spectroscopic intermediate, not solubility)
Table 4: fit equations of calibration curves: model parameters
Tables 9 and 10: deviations from Duan and Akinfiev-Diamond models: derived
